new_statements.rule_in_words: Ongamo is described as a tone language with four surface tones (high, low, mid, high-falling); the same tones are recorded for Maasai, where they are lexically and grammatically relevant, and Vossen 1981 (p. 50) adds that nominal case is marked by tone in Ongamo-Maa. No source opened says anything about word stress or accent; the reading is 'tonal, silent on stress'.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Vossen warns (p. 195) that 'linguistic data on On are still scanty' and that Heine & Vossen's material contains irregularities, and (1981: 46) that tone-marking in the comparative wordlist is 'in most cases tentative'.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns surface tones on lexical items (Vossen's data conventions: nouns in the singular, verbs in the infinitive); no word-vs-phrase domain is discussed and no stress is mentioned. Data are Heine & Vossen's 1975 field notes plus Fleming 1965 and Ehret 1967/1971/1974 wordlists.
new_statements.identity_note: Ngasa = Ongamo (speakers' own name oŋgamo, sg. oŋgamoni), also Kingasa/Kingassa/Ongamoi/Shaka; Glottolog ngas1238, ISO nsg. Vossen 1982 labels it 'Ongamo (On)' and treats it as a single language with no dialect division; no identity problem.
